issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or won't move in gear
issues.sym: Shifts slip or flare, the car hesitates between gears, it gets stuck in one gear, or it will not move at all when put in Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in these Galants wears internally as the miles add up. Owners report slipping, lock-ups and debris in the fluid, often somewhere between 70,000 and 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for a burnt smell or dark color. If it is slipping or won't engage, avoid hard driving and get a transmission diagnosis; a rebuild or a used or remanufactured unit is the usual fix.

issues.t: Transmission stuck in one gear or slipping on later models
issues.sym: The transmission slips, shifts late or harshly, or suddenly stays in one gear. On some cars a gear indicator light flashes and the car feels very sluggish.
issues.why: Owners of the 2004-2012 Galant report internal transmission failures; one documented case involved a broken snap ring and wave spring that clogged the filter. The computer then locks the transmission in a fail-safe gear.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. If the car is stuck in one gear, drive gently and only as far as a shop. A rebuild is often needed once internal parts have broken.

issues.t: Oil pump failure and low oil pressure
issues.sym: The oil pressure light flickers or stays on, the engine gets noisy, or it loses power. Left alone, the engine can be badly damaged.
issues.why: CarComplaints lists a failed oil pump as one of the worst problems for this generation, usually around 100,000 miles. Without full oil pressure the bearings and valvetrain wear quickly.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off. Check the oil level, then have oil pressure tested before driving further.

issues.t: Catalytic converter failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, a rotten-egg smell, sluggish acceleration, a rattle under the car, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Catalytic converters on these Galants commonly wear out around 100,000 miles. Misfires or oil burning can speed up the damage.
issues.next: Have the codes read and fix any misfire first. Then have the converter tested before you replace it; a new one will fail again if the root cause is still there.

issues.t: No heat or clicking from the temperature control
issues.sym: The heater blows cold or lukewarm air, or you hear clicking behind the dash when you turn the temperature knob.
issues.why: The temperature control motor (blend door actuator) or the heater control valve fails, so hot coolant never reaches the cabin air. This was the most common complaint on the 2002 Galant.
issues.next: Check the coolant level first. If it is full, have the blend door actuator and heater valve tested; both are usually simple part swaps.

issues.t: Power window falls into the door or stops working
issues.sym: A window drops down inside the door, moves crooked, makes grinding noises, or stops going up and down.
issues.why: The window regulator cables or clips break, and moisture inside the door can ruin the motor or switch. Windows were the most-reported category on the 2003 Galant.
issues.next: Tape the glass up or cover the opening to keep rain out, then have the regulator replaced. Replacing just the regulator is usually cheaper than the regulator and motor together.

issues.t: Warped front rotors and fast brake wear
issues.sym: The steering wheel or brake pedal shakes when stopping, or the brakes squeal or grind. Owners report replacing pads and rotors well before 40,000 miles.
issues.why: The front rotors and pads on these Galants wear and warp quickly, especially with frequent hard stops, and some owners also report rear brakes out of adjustment.
issues.next: Have the pads and rotors measured. Replacing both together with good-quality parts, and torquing the wheels correctly, gives the best result.

issues.t: Lower ball joints can wear and separate (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from the front over bumps, wandering steering, or uneven tire wear. In the worst case a ball joint separates and a front wheel folds under.
issues.why: Torn rubber boots let dirt and water into the lower ball joints, which then rust and wear. Mitsubishi recalled the cars to inspect, seal or replace the joints (campaign 00V421).
issues.next: Check with a Mitsubishi dealer that the recall was done. If you hear clunking, have the ball joints checked right away; many cars are past the recall work and need new joints.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley breaks apart
issues.sym: A sudden loud noise from the engine, the belts coming off, a battery light, and loss of power steering.
issues.why: The rubber layer in the crankshaft pulley (harmonic balancer) can separate with age, letting the outer ring and belts fly off. Owners of 1998 Galants reported this happening while driving.
issues.next: If you see the pulley wobbling or cracked rubber, have it replaced before it fails. A failed pulley can also damage the timing belt, so have that checked at the same time.

issues.t: Headlights and dash lights dimming
issues.sym: The headlights and dash lights go dim while driving, often at night, and may brighten again with engine speed.
issues.why: Owners traced this to the charging system and wiring, and some found that a new alternator alone did not cure it. Weak grounds and worn connections are common on cars this old.
issues.next: Have the battery, alternator output and the main ground cables tested. Cleaning and tightening the grounds is cheap and often helps.

issues.t: Stalling or no-start from the crankshaft position sensor
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, or it stalls while driving and may restart after it cools down. The tachometer may drop to zero.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor or its wiring fails, so the computer loses its timing signal and cuts spark and fuel.
issues.next: Note when it happens (hot or cold). Have the codes read; a scan tool can often catch the sensor dropping out. The sensor itself is a low-cost part.

issues.t: Steering gear nut can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Steering wheel vibration, stiff steering, or trouble turning left.
issues.why: A nut inside the steering gear could work loose. Mitsubishi recalled 2000 Galants to inspect it and replace the steering gear if needed (campaign 00V225).
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to confirm the recall was done. If the steering feels odd, don't drive the car until it is checked.

issues.t: Battery cable harness heat damage (recall)
issues.sym: No-start, A/C not working, turn signals acting up, or the oil pressure warning misbehaving.
issues.why: On V6 cars, heat from the exhaust can cook the battery cable harness and short circuits. Mitsubishi added heat protection or replaced the harness (campaign 99V333).
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall was completed. Look for melted or brittle wiring near the exhaust manifold.

issues.t: Turn signal and wiper stalks can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals don't cancel or work properly, headlights stay on, washers keep spraying, or the wipers stop.
issues.why: The steering column switch levers can loosen or crack. Mitsubishi installed a redesigned switch under recall 99V305.
issues.next: Check the recall status with a dealer. If the stalks feel loose, have the switch replaced.

issues.t: Transmission cooler hose can leak (recall)
issues.sym: Red fluid under the front of the car, shifting problems, or smoke if fluid drips on the exhaust.
issues.why: A poorly made transmission oil cooler hose can weaken and leak. Mitsubishi replaced the hose assembly under recall 01V011.
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. Check under the car for red fluid and keep the transmission fluid topped up until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power steering tube rubs and leaks on V6 (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, whining from the pump, heavier steering, or a burning smell.
issues.why: The power steering feed tube can rub against an exhaust heat shield and wear through. Fluid on hot parts can start a fire. Mitsubishi rerouted the tube under recall 01V295.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the recall. If you see a leak or smell burning fluid, stop driving until it is inspected.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key can be pulled out of the ignition while the shifter is not in Park, so the car could roll away.
issues.why: The ignition key interlock cable can let its cam slide while driving. Mitsubishi inspected and corrected about 73,000 Galants (campaign 08V276).
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and have a dealer check the recall status.

issues.t: Fuel tank strap bracket can split (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. In a severe crash with a full tank, the tank could drop and leak fuel.
issues.why: A rear fuel tank strap bracket may have a split from a stamping defect. Dealers inspect it and reinforce it if needed (campaign 08V454).
issues.next: Check with a Mitsubishi dealer that the recall was done.

issues.t: Transmission oil cooler pipe can rust through (recall)
issues.sym: Transmission fluid leaking near the front of the car, possible smoke or a burning smell.
issues.why: The cooler pipe on some 2010 Galants did not get enough anti-rust plating. If it rusts through, fluid can leak onto hot parts. Dealers replace the pipe (campaign 10V066).
issues.next: Have the recall checked by VIN. If you see a leak, stop driving and have it inspected.

issues.t: Airbag (SRS) warning light on or airbag faults
issues.sym: The SRS airbag light stays on. Owners also report airbags not deploying in crashes, or the passenger airbag cover coming loose.
issues.why: Airbag and seat belt complaints are the most common NHTSA reports for the later Galant. Wiring, sensors or the control unit can fault and switch the system off.
issues.next: Have the SRS codes read promptly. While the light is on, the airbags may not work in a crash.

issues.t: Fuel filler neck breaks or leaks
issues.sym: A fuel smell around the car, fuel dripping under the rear while filling up, or a check engine light for an EVAP leak.
issues.why: The fuel filler neck and its connections can crack or rust, letting fuel and vapor escape. CarComplaints lists a broken filler neck on the 2004 Galant around 60,000 miles.
issues.next: Fuel leaks are a fire risk. Have it inspected soon, and do not overfill the tank.

issues.t: Overheating from water pump or intake manifold leaks
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, coolant level drops, or you see coolant under the front of the car. Some owners report the engine shutting down.
issues.why: The water pump can leak or fail, and owners also report cracked intake manifolds near the throttle body. On the V6, the water pump is driven by the timing belt.
issues.next: Stop driving if it overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test done. On V6 cars, replace the timing belt along with the water pump.

issues.t: Fuel vapor (EVAP) system failure
issues.sym: A check engine light, sometimes with a fuel smell or trouble filling the tank.
issues.why: Parts of the evaporative emissions system, which traps fuel vapor from the tank, fail. CarComplaints lists this on the 2000 Galant around 50,000 miles.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap clicks tight, then have the EVAP codes read and the system smoke-tested.

issues.t: Paint fading and peeling
issues.sym: The paint turns chalky, fades or peels off the roof, hood and trunk, most often on black or dark cars.
issues.why: The clear coat breaks down in the sun. Owners of 1998-2006 Galants reported it, often after their warranty claims were turned down.
issues.next: Wash and wax regularly and park in shade when you can. Once the clear coat is peeling, only sanding and repainting the panel fixes it.

issues.t: Underbody rust
issues.sym: Rust on the underside of the car, around the subframe and suspension mounts.
issues.why: Owners report early undercarriage corrosion, especially where roads are salted in winter.
issues.next: Rinse the underside in winter and have rust spots treated early. Have rusty suspension parts checked at each inspection.
